title: God of Eternity! from Thee
description: God of Eternity! from Thee in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 565, “Close of the Year”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God of e-ter-ni-ty! from Thee Did in-fant time his be-ing draw; Mo-ments and days, and months and years, Re-volve by Thine un-var-ied law.

lines: Did infant time his being draw;
Moments and days, and months and years,
Silent and swift they glide away:
Steady and strong the current flows,
The boundless gulf from which it rose.
Great Source of wisdom! teach our hearts
To know the price of every hour,
That time may bear us on to joys
Beyond its measure and its power.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
